Title: NST Leader: Making Sarawak's Flying Doctor Service safer
Article:
Malaysians gripe about practically everything, but almost everyone appreciates our heavily subsidised petrol and public healthcare system.
If there are gripes about the system, it's about the long wait, overcrowding and high demand. It's inevitable because some 90 per cent of Malaysians live within 5km of a government hospital or clinic.
So, spare a thought for citizens in need of medical care in rural villages, jungles and remote regions.
Malaysia's healthcare for all philosophy is driven by a collective social duty regardless of wealth, political inclination or social status.
This makes the Flying Doctor Service remarkable. The tragic helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Sarawak, that killed a pilot and four healthcare workers reminds us that healthcare revolves not only around hospitals and clinics.
The entire rural healthcare delivery system needs to be reexamined.
The Flying Doctor Service, introduced in 1973 to deliver healthcare to indigenous and rural communities, provides general treatment, maternal and child healthcare and childhood immunisations.
It serves 14,830 residents in 85 remote locations, flying out every one to three months, depending on weather and scheduling.
The tragedy has temporarily grounded operations, but the downtime gives the Health Ministry the opportunity for an urgent review of the service.
As alternative land and water routes are being explored, the Flying Doctor Service has to re-examine safety, especially the reliability of the helicopters it uses, most of which are decades old.
The review will focus on the aircraft, contracts, maintenance, operational procedures and overall delivery model.
In the mean time, medical attention in the interior cannot be neglected for weeks or even days. The Flying Doctor Service cannot depend too much on helicopters.
The ideal would be to have a network of boats, four-wheel-drives, mobile clinics and military and emergency service assets. Already, the police, air force, Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency and Fire and Rescue Department are chipping in with mercy flights until investigations are concluded.
Rural clinics and mobile healthcare teams can also reduce emergency evacuations. With better digital connectivity, telemedicine services can also connect rural clinics and community health workers with specialists from major hospitals.
The Flying Doctor Service's commercial contracts on procurement, contractor selection and terms governing private helicopter operators also need a relook.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia is expected to audit the maintenance history, safety protocols and airworthiness of the crashed Bo 105 helicopter manufactured in 1991.
Given the risks of the job, the Health Ministry should increase allowances for the personnel involved. It is stuck at RM30 per trip.
Provide mandatory, government-funded insurance coverage, too.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump says US has tools to keep AI safe, concerns are part of 'sick conspiracy'
Article:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump said on Monday that the United States already has guardrails in place to regulate and prosecute AI companies, appearing to play down concerns expressed by industry leaders over the weekend about misuse of artificial intelligence.
"The only control or 'guardrails' that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!" Trump wrote on Truth Social, adding that China would benefit from the doubt being cast on artificial intelligence development.
"We already have tremendous CRIMINAL and REGULATORY power over these companies! There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China."
Public concerns about the potential harm from AI grew in the US after two Anthropic researchers issued warnings last week that the rapidly progressing technology could lead to the extinction of the human race ‌in the not-too-distant future.
On Saturday, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei outlined a three-step framework intended to pace development and create more time to manage its risks. The proposal was immediately endorsed by several other executives at major AI companies, including Elon Musk, who runs xAI, and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman.
Trump said the tools intended to keep AI safe had already been used on Amodei.
"The Trump Administration has stopped AI 'people' from doing bad, or potentially bad, 'things,' like Dario (Anthropic!), who is now pretending to be a 'perfect little angel' - and we will continue to do so," he said.
Trump has resisted stirring concerns about AI and has largely embraced AI firms in his second term.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cat-astrophe averted: Public help scoop three tonnes of 'ikan keli' off the road
Article:
BESUT: Members of the public rallied to help collect three tonnes of African catfish that had spilt onto a road near a secondary school in Kampung Padang Luas here yesterday, saving the fish from certain death.
The fish, which were being transported to a newly opened fishing pond near Pelagat for a fishing competition scheduled on Sept 19, were strewn across the road after the lorry carrying them hit a road hump.
Hamimi Shahira Nor Sanadi, 29, the sister-in-law of the fish supplier, said kind-hearted members of the public helped collect the fish and returned them to the lorry driver.
"The fish were all collected and handed back to the driver by around noon.
"No fish died in the incident, but some were injured and have since been placed in another pond to recover," she said.
Hamimi said the incident was believed to have occurred about 8am when the lorry, hired to transport the fish belonging to her brother-in-law, Che Suhaimi Che Rahim, 33, hit a road hump.
"The impact caused the lorry's rear gate to break, and the fish spilt onto the road.
"The driver was initially unaware of what had happened. He only realised the fish were missing when he arrived at the new pond and had to rush back to the scene," she said.
She said the exact losses suffered by Che Suhaimi cannot be determined yet, although he would have to replace some of the fish for the fishing competition.
The incident went viral on social media, prompting a range of reactions and speculation.
"Some claimed the fish had come out of the drains and onto the road, while others even thought the images were AI-generated.
"Some of the information being shared was inaccurate, which is why I decided to come forward and explain what really happened," she said.

Title: Anwar heads to Maldives after BRICS summit, India engagements
Article:
KERALAM : Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim departed Keralam for an official visit to the Maldives today after completing his five‑day working visit to India.
The aircraft carrying the Prime Minister left Calicut International Airport at 7.26pm local time (9.56pm Malaysian time) for Velana International Airport in Male.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, is accompanied by Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan.
In Male, Anwar and Maldives President Dr Mohamed Muizzu are scheduled to assess bilateral ties, exchange views on regional and international issues, and witness the signing of memoranda of understanding (MoUs) on defence cooperation and Islamic affairs.
Earlier, the Prime Minister met Keralam Chief Minister V. D. Satheesan and Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar to discuss cooperation in trade, investment, tourism, healthcare and education.
Anwar arrived in New Delhi on Friday to attend the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit hosted by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Diplomatic relations between Malaysia and India were established in 1957, shortly after independence. India remains Malaysia's largest trading partner in South Asia, with bilateral trade reaching US$18.55 billion (RM79.33 billion) in 2025.– BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar's Kishore Kumar rendition goes viral as BRICS visit boosts diplomatic, economic ties
Article:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's rendition of Kishore Kumar's classic
"Khwab Ho Tum Ya Koi Haqeeqat"
went viral in India, adding a soft‑diplomacy touch to his participation in the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit.
The 92‑second video drew positive reactions online, with many calling it a "mic drop" moment and the "sweetest part" of the gathering. The cultural gesture highlighted Malaysia–India ties while Anwar's summit focus remained on strengthening diplomacy, investment and economic cooperation.
SOFT DIPLOMACY
The viral moment underscored Anwar's distinctive soft diplomacy. He often lightens tense settings with humour while ensuring key issues are addressed.
"I know this is very late. It takes only a young man with a steady and firm position to be able to conduct a meeting this late. Thank you very much," he quipped to Russian President Vladimir Putin during a bilateral meeting past 11pm on Sept 11.
At 79, Anwar's remark eased the formal air with Putin, 73.
He also embraced Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, saying: "My brother. So happy to meet you."
Similar warmth marked meetings with Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El‑Sisi, Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto, Kazakhstan President Kassym‑Jomart Tokayev and Uzbekistan Deputy Prime Minister Jamshid Kuchkarov. He also met UN Secretary‑General António Guterres and WTO Director‑General Ngozi Okonjo‑Iweala.
ON GAZA, MIDDLE EAST AND A FAIRER GLOBAL FINANCIAL SYSTEM
Anwar used the summit to strengthen bilateral ties, exchange views on regional issues and push for reform. He raised the humanitarian crisis in Gaza and tensions in Middle East, urging unity to stop bloodshed and achieve a lasting solution.
He also discussed haze from forest fires in Kalimantan and Sumatra with Prabowo, noting its impact on Malaysia.
In his National Statement, Anwar called for a fairer global financing system.
"Many countries were facing debt distress or were at serious risk of it, with some spending more on interest payments than on educating their young or caring for the sick. No nation should be forced to choose between honouring its debts and honouring its obligations to its people," he stressed.
Malaysia also supports reducing reliance on the US dollar in trade, encouraging use of local currencies.
Anwar met representatives of DRB‑Hicom, Segula Technologies India, AWL Agri Business Ltd and Motherson Group to explore investment opportunities.
KERALAM VISIT, AWARD AND CALL TO EMBRACE AI
In Kozhikode, Keralam, Anwar met Grand Mufti Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad at Jamia Markaz, discussing community development, education and interfaith harmony.
He received the inaugural Sheikh Abu Bakar Foundation Excellence Award for five decades of public service, education, Islamic scholarship and international dialogue.
At the "Gathering of Honour for the Prime Minister of Malaysia," Anwar urged the Muslim world to embrace AI and modern technology while preserving values.
Speaking before 2,000 attendees, he said: "Muslim scholars and societies could not afford to remain detached from the rapid development of AI and modern technology, as a lack of knowledge and understanding could leave them vulnerable to external influences."
He also met Chief Minister V. D. Satheesan, encouraging collaboration in digital economy, healthcare, tourism and education, and invited him to visit Malaysia.
Further meetings included the UAE‑India Business Council, UAE‑based BEEAH Group, Keralam Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arleka and Industries Minister P.K. Kunhalikutty, alongside industry leaders.
Anwar highlighted Malaysia–Keralam's longstanding ties in trade, migration, education and culture, and called for deeper cooperation in high‑value sectors.
Anwar's visit — his second to India as Prime Minister — showcased both cultural resonance and strategic diplomacy. From India, he heads to the Maldives for a two‑day official visit. - BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar: BRICS not against other blocs, Malaysia pushing for fairer global order
Article:
KERALAM : Malaysia's participation in the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit is not aimed at opposing any bloc but at advocating a fairer international system and rules, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He stressed Malaysia will maintain good ties with the United States, European Union (EU), Australia and other partners while pushing for reform of outdated global structures.
"BRICS or Asean is not meant to oppose other groups. Our cooperation with the EU, US and Australia continues. We are only setting fair rules. The UN system agreed in 1945 is outdated, unfair and undemocratic," he told Malaysian media in Calicut before concluding his working visit to India.
Anwar said Malaysia must maintain good bilateral relations with the US but should not be prevented from voicing views important for Malaysia, the region and the world.
He added that the international system, including the World Bank and IMF, must be reviewed as some aspects no longer reflect current needs and realities.
Malaysia also supports reducing reliance on the US dollar in trade, including using local currencies for transactions between countries.
On full BRICS membership, Anwar said a moratorium is in place, but Malaysia's partner status allows participation in almost all activities and mechanisms.
"They were kind enough to accept Malaysia as a partner country early. In practice, the working mechanism does not restrict us from joining almost all activities, and we have done so," he said.
Malaysia has been a BRICS partner country since Jan 1, 2025. Anwar attended the summit in New Delhi hosted by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, delivering Malaysia's National Statement on Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth.– BERNAMA

Title: Missed out? Expired plate numbers could be back on the market
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Road Transport Department (RTD) is developing a new feature for its JPJeBid platform that will allow expired vehicle registration numbers to be offered to the public again.
RTD director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli said the initiative would cover registration numbers which had previously been successfully bid for or sold but were not registered to a vehicle within the stipulated period.
He said registration numbers generally came with a specified validity period, including six or 12 months depending on the approval, within which they must be registered to a vehicle.
"After that period, the number will return to the RTD system. When these numbers expire, we will release them again and offer them back to the public," he said after launching the H series Special Registration Number in conjunction with Malaysia Day 2026 at Menara 118.
Aedy said the department was currently finalising the mechanism, standard operating procedures and system for the initiative, which is expected to be introduced to the public within the next two to three months.
He said the initiative would involve expanding the existing system, while further details on how members of the public could obtain the re-offered numbers would be announced later.
Aedy said the prices of the re-offered numbers would not be based on their previous winning bid prices.
Instead, prices would be determined according to the respective registration number categories.
"These numbers have certain prices which we set according to their categories. Popular numbers will have a different price, while attractive numbers will have another price," he said.
During his presentation, Aedy said special registration number series had generated millions of ringgit in government revenue in recent years.
The GOLD, FFF, EV, PETRA and MADANI series generated RM45,931,252 in 2024, while special series introduced in 2025 generated RM62,905,977.
For 2026, the FH, P_P and V_MY series have so far generated RM38,832,936.

Title: Anwar: Najib pardon decision guided by law, Constitution and due process
Article:
KERALAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim says the deferment of former premier Datuk Seri Najib Razak's pardon petition was made based on the rule of law, constitutional principles and official advice.
He said his role in the Pardons Board meeting was subject to law and guidance from the Attorney General.
"A prime minister must give views based on the law, advice from the Attorney General and the rules. That is what I did. However, this remains within the discretion of the Yang di‑Pertuan Agong (His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia), who must take all factors into consideration," he told Malaysian media in Calicut before concluding his working visit to India.
Anwar said Najib's pardon issue should not be viewed personally but assessed through law and governance.
"We must submit to the rule of law and the Constitution. I have never taken a prejudiced or hateful stance," he said.
He added that political considerations and Umno's firm views were noted, but he chose to act on principles.
"I know the easy way and the difficult way, but I chose the path I believe is right, following law and governance," he said.
Last Friday, Sultan Ibrahim consented to Najib's petition being deferred to a future Pardons Board meeting.
The Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister's Department confirmed the decision after the 63rd Pardons Board Meeting for the Federal Territories at Istana Negara on Sept 11.
On Dec 26 last year, the High Court sentenced Najib to 15 years in prison and fined him RM11.4 billion after convicting him of four charges of abuse of power and 21 charges of money laundering involving RM2.3 billion from 1MDB funds.– BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar: Moderate approach on Umno issue needed to keep unity government stable
Article:
KERALAM:  Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim says he has chosen a moderate approach in handling differing views on cooperation with Umno within the unity government to ensure stability.
Anwar, who is also Pakatan Harapan chairman, stressed that harsh actions could harm the country. "I choose a moderate path because what is important is that the government must be stable, otherwise there will be many losses," he said at a press conference with Malaysian media in Calicut before concluding his working visit to India.
He added that differing views among parties, including PH, are normal in a coalition and should not be seen as threatening cooperation. "We listen to everything, but to my knowledge, I don't see any problems. There are small and normal ones. Even in a household, there are minor issues, let alone with political commanders," he said.
Anwar was commenting on issues raised at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.– BERNAMA

Title: Two 12-year-old boys die after falling into drain in Kulim
Article:
KULIM: Two 12-year-old boys were killed after falling into a drain, while two others were injured in an incident at Taman Desa Kayangan, Sungai Karangan, here tonight.
The two injured children, aged eight and 11, were taken to hospital following the incident at 7.30pm.
Kulim district police chief Superintendent Syamsul Sinring confirmed the incident, according to BuletinTV3.
"Members of the Sungai Karangan police station went to the scene and found that two boys had been taken to hospital, while two others had died at the scene," he said in an initial statement issued earlier.

Title: 500 green sea turtle hatchlings released in Terengganu
Article:
KERTIH: A total of 500 one-day-old green sea turtle hatchlings, each measuring 2.5cm, were released into the sea at the Ma' Daerah Turtle Sanctuary Centre in Kertih here today.
The release was part of conservation efforts under the 2026 Sustainable Environment Programme organised by the Terengganu Girl Guides Association of Malaysia.
Regent of Terengganu Tengku Muhammad Ismail Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin also released several turtle hatchlings at about 6.30pm.
Tengku Puteri Daulath Raja Tengku Fatimatuz Zahra', Tengku Muhammad Ismail's sister, was also in attendance.
Also present were Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar and Terengganu Fisheries Department director Pang Nyukang.
The sanctuary incubated the green sea turtle hatchlings, and the release aimed to support the species' survival and raise public awareness of the importance of turtle conservation in the state.
Earlier, Tengku Muhammad Ismail called on the public to help protect the environment and marine ecosystems to ensure the sustainability of natural resources for future generations.
He said these efforts were important as pollution, littering and uncontrolled human activities increasingly threatened the balance of the environment and marine life, including fish, turtles and coral reefs.
"Protecting the environment is not solely the responsibility of the government or certain organisations. It is a shared responsibility. Although our individual actions may seem small, when taken by millions of people, their impact can be significant," Tengku Muhammad Ismail said.

Title: [UPDATED] RTD launches 'H' special registration number series for Malaysia Day
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The letter "H", which the Road Transport Department (RTD) associates with harmony, has been launched as a Special Registration Number series for Malaysia Day on Sept 16.
The announcement was made by RTD director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli at the launch of the Special Registration Number series in conjunction with Malaysia Day 2026 at Menara 118 here today.
The special registration numbers will be available from H1 to H9999.
Aedy said the H series was particularly significant as the single-letter registration prefix had never previously been offered by the department.
He said bidding for the series would open on Sept 16 and close on Sept 20, with the results to be announced on Sept 21.
"The H series is synonymous with harmony and the harmony of our country.
"In conjunction with Malaysia Day, we are offering this final single-letter series in Malaysia to be offered by the RTD and the Malaysian government.
"After this, there will be no more single-letter series to be offered by the RTD. This is a very special registration number series and Malaysians should take the opportunity to bid for it," he told reporters after launching the special registration number series today.
Asked about the association of the letter H with taxis, Aedy said taxi registration numbers were paired with state registration prefixes and were therefore distinct from the standalone H series.
He said, for example, HA had previously been used for taxis registered in Perak, while HB was used for taxis registered in Selangor.
"However, there has never been a series offering a single H.
"We are of the view that this single H does not belong to any particular party. It belongs to the Malaysian government and we are releasing it for Malaysians to own," he said.
Aedy said the RTD would also not open bidding for other registration number series during the H-series bidding period.
During his presentation, Aedy said the RTD's special registration number series had generated substantial revenue for the government over the past three years.
In 2024, the special GOLD, FFF, EV, PETRA and MADANI series generated a total of RM45,931,252.
This increased to RM62,905,977 in 2025, when several special series were introduced, including SIS, GM and ANSARA.
In 2026, the FH, P_P and V_MY series have so far generated RM38,832,936.

Title: Foong family seeks Hexza MGO exemption
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Chemicals industry specialist Hexza Corp Bhd is seeking an exemption for the Foong family from undertaking a mandatory general offer (MGO).
This is because the company's proposed dividend reinvestment could push their collective stake above the takeover threshold.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Hexza said the exemption is required because the shareholders intend to reinvest their final dividend entitlement into new shares.
This will potentially increase their combined shareholding beyond the 33 per cent threshold that triggers an MGO.
The Foong family currently holds 67.72 million shares, or 32.94 per cent of Hexza, including a 30.62 per cent stake held through Summit Holdings.
Datuk Dr Foong Weng Cheong is a shareholder, while his son Foong Leon Chiew is the company's executive chairman.
Hexza has proposed a final dividend of 7.5 sen per share for the financial year ended June 30, 2026, with the full amount eligible for reinvestment under its dividend reinvestment plan (DRP), subject to approval.
If the major shareholders reinvest their full entitlement while other shareholders opt for cash, their collective stake could rise to 34.90 per cent, based on an illustrative issue price of 82 sen.
Under the maximum scenario of 66 sen per share, the stake could increase to 35.36 per cent.
The shareholders have stated that they do not intend to make an MGO for the remaining Hexza shares.
The company will therefore seek an exemption from the Securities Commission, subject to approval by non-interested shareholders at an extraordinary general meeting.
The interested shareholders and directors will abstain from voting, while independent adviser cfSolutions Sdn Bhd has been appointed to advise non-interested shareholders.
Bursa Malaysia has approved the listing of up to 20.5 million new shares under the second DRP, subject to conditions.
The exemption is expected to be completed by the first quarter of 2027.
Hexza said the proposal will not affect its share capital, net assets, gearing, earnings or earnings per share, although the DRP could dilute EPS depending on participation.
The company reported a more than six-fold rise in FY2026 net profit to RM3 million, while revenue grew 25.4 per cent to RM74.35 million.

Title: Factory bus crashes into drain in Penang, driver injured [WATCH]
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A factory bus driver was injured after the vehicle crashed through a road divider and plunged into a three-metre-deep drain.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director John Sagun Francis said the 49-year-old driver was trapped in the bus when firefighters arrived at the scene near the Jalan Tun Dr Awang roundabout at 6.11pm.
"The victim was trapped inside the bus and was successfully extricated," he said.
The driver was taken to Penang Hospital.

Title: BMS Holdings eyes northern state expansion with Penang partner
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: BMS Holdings Bhd is proposing to form a 60:40 joint venture (JV) with the shareholders of Penang-based Wee Tatt Traders Sdn Bhd to expand its tile and building materials distribution network in northern states.
In a filing to Bursa Malaysia, BMS said it signed a letter of intent with Wee Tatt shareholders Tan Kar Seng, Tan Hooi Ling and Chiew Bee Hong for the proposed JV.
The JV company will be known as Jubin BMS (Wee Tatt) Sdn Bhd or another name approved by the Companies Commission of Malaysia.
It will trade, distribute, market, supply and sell tiles, ceramic and porcelain products, sanitary ware, building materials and related products.
BMS will contribute RM3 million in cash for its 60 per cent stake, while the Wee Tatt shareholders will contribute RM2 million worth of inventory.
The shareholders will also procure the transfer of Wee Tatt's business to the JV as a going concern, including agreed inventories, assets, employees, customer contracts and supplier arrangements.
The RM3 million contribution will be funded through internally generated funds and/or bank borrowings.
Wee Tatt is principally involved in trading ceramics, online retail and general trading, with operations mainly in Penang.
BMS said the JV will enable it to leverage Wee Tatt's existing operations and market presence to strengthen its reach in the northern states.
The parties intend to execute the shareholders' agreement and other definitive agreements in 30 working days.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Oil prices continue surge, rising 3pct amid Saudi pipeline outage after attack
Article:
LONDON: Oil prices continued their surge on Monday, rising more than three per cent after fresh strikes on Saudi Arabian energy infrastructure and attacks on ships in the Middle East heightened supply concerns.
Brent crude futures climbed US$3, or 2.9 per cent, to US$107.61 a barrel by 1112 GMT, after earlier hitting a session high of US$108.65. WTI futures gained US$2.48, or 2.5 per cent, to US$102.53 a barrel.
Oil prices surged about nine per cent last week as attacks in the Middle East escalated, with Brent rising above US$100 a barrel for the first time since July and hitting its highest since May at around US$110.
The rally pushed US diesel prices above US$6 a gallon for the first time, prompting US President Donald Trump to urge Ukraine to stop attacking Russian diesel infrastructure.
Global bond markets have come under pressure as higher energy prices fuel inflation and interest rates, with yields repeatedly climbing to fresh multi-year highs.
Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline was temporarily shut following a drone attack, according to Saudi officials. The shutdown threatens up to four per cent of global oil supply and limits Saudi Arabia's ability to bypass the Strait of Hormuz and reroute exports through the Bab el-Mandeb strait.
With the pipeline out of service, the port of Yanbu on the Red Sea has enough inventory to cover only five to seven days of exports, according to three industry sources.
"The relatively contained price reaction suggests the market still expects Saudi inventories to cushion exports in the near term, but if the disruption extends beyond the five-to-seven-day inventory cushion, that could change quickly," said Janiv Shah, oil markets analyst at Rystad.
Meanwhile, Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis reached the strategic island of Perim on Friday as they moved to tighten their control over Bab el-Mandeb.
In the Strait of Hormuz, a vessel was struck by a projectile, causing a fire and forcing its crew to evacuate, the British maritime security agency UKMTO said on Sunday.
Iran said one person was killed and four crew members were wounded aboard an Iranian commercial vessel struck off its coast.
A scheduled Monday meeting in Oman between Gulf countries and Iran to discuss the Strait of Hormuz was postponed, Oman's foreign minister said, dampening hopes of improved shipping.
Meanwhile, Iran issued a list of 77 ships it said had violated its protocols for operating in Hormuz.
"Short of stopping both oil price affecting wars and curing the global refinery (capacity) problem, our fraternity is wondering where an inoculation against $120 Brent can be found," said PVM analyst John Evans, pointing to Russian refinery outages and falling stockpiles.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Remand extended for 5 held over forged vehicle transfer documents
Article:
IPOH: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has obtained a four-day remand extension for five people believed to have acted as middlemen for a syndicate that falsified vehicle ownership transfer documents and allegedly bribed enforcement officers in Perak.
Magistrate A Hafiizh Abu Bakar granted the extension until Sept 18 after allowing MACC's application at the Ipoh magistrate's court this morning, following the expiry of the suspects' initial remand.
The five suspects, four men and one woman, were initially remanded for six days from last Wednesday.
Perak MACC director Datuk Azizul Ahmad Sarkawi confirmed the extension when contacted.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 18 of the MACC Act 2009.
The five are among
11 individuals arrested
in an investigation into a syndicate that allegedly forged vehicle ownership transfer documents and bribed enforcement officers to facilitate fraudulent transfers.
The suspects comprise seven men and four women aged between 30 and 40.
The suspects, five agents and six Road Transport Department (RTD) personnel, were arrested while giving their statements at the Perak MACC office.
The suspects allegedly conspired to submit falsified documents to the RTD for vehicle ownership transfers involving 16 registration numbers.
Initial investigations found that the offence took place in 2025, with the agents suspected of conspiring with civil servants to submit the falsified documents.
The documents were believed to have been used to facilitate illegal vehicle ownership transfers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia stronger today after major fiscal reforms – SC chairman
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is in a stronger position than a decade ago, thanks to major fiscal decisions by the government, such as subsidy cuts and a focus on economic development, said Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) chairman Datuk Mohammad Faiz Azmi.
He said the country's improved financial position was also reflected in the recent pricing of its US dollar Government Sukuk issuance, which demonstrated stronger international recognition.
"Malaysia already offers a deep and diversified capital market which is bigger than banking assets, recognised leadership in Islamic finance, sound regulatory and governance foundations, as well as having a firm commitment to strengthening cross-border connectivity," he said at the Asean Investment Roadshow today.
Mohammad Faiz said efforts to improve the vibrancy and growth of Malaysia's capital market were being undertaken under the Capital Market Masterplan 2026-2030 (CMP), including through initiatives such as MY Value Up with Bursa Malaysia involving the country's top 88 public-listed companies.
The SC had also recently signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Hong Kong Securities and Futures Commission to establish a framework for single-prospectus dual-listed initial public offerings and cross-listing of eligible REITs and ETFs, aimed at widening market access, providing more options for issuers and investors and deepening cross-border participation.
Mohammad Faiz also said Asean regulators had agreed last year on five key initiatives, including pursuing consistent voluntary carbon market standards and implementing the Asean Taxonomy Version 4.
The initiatives also included issuing a simplified environmental, social and governance (ESG) disclosure guide for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Asean and developing a project guide to identify pilot projects for blended finance for adaptation and resilience funding.
He said the Asean Capital Markets Forum (ACMF) Action Plan 2026-2030 comprised five strategic thrusts, 11 key priorities and 18 initiatives aimed at strengthening regional integration and Asean's global positioning.
"Four key initiatives in the ACMF Action Plan related to strengthening regional integration and global positioning are to promote Asean Diamonds, facilitate the creation of Asean indices, create a renewed focus on Islamic Finance, which is a differentiator for our markets, with a better shariah screening tool, and to facilitate intra-Asean activities, products and connectivity," said Mohammad Faiz.
He said a key priority was to establish a committee to promote Asean as an asset class, currently led by the Philippines and Singapore.
Greater regional connectivity and international participation would be crucial to Asean's next phase of growth, while calling on investors to reconsider Asean as a strategic long-term investment destination, said Mohammad Faiz.

Title: Quarry worker killed when boulder falls onto lorry in Ipoh [WATCH]
Article:
IPOH: A 53-year-old quarry worker was killed when a boulder fell onto the lorry he was driving at a quarry in Keramat Pulai here today.
The victim, identified as M. Sivakumar, was trapped in the lorry following the incident at the quarry in Keramat Pulai, Kampung Kepayang.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department operations chief Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the department received a distress call at 5.18pm.
He said firefighters from the Simpang Pulai and Gopeng Fire and Rescue stations arrived at the scene at 5.29pm.
"Initial information indicated that a lorry carrying quarry rocks was crushed by a boulder while quarrying work was being carried out.
"The victim was trapped inside the lorry and was later pronounced dead at the scene by Health Ministry personnel," he said in a statement today.
He said firefighters used hydraulic equipment to extricate the victim.
He said Sivakumar was removed from the lorry before his remains were handed over to police.
A total of 12 firefighters were involved in the operation.

Title: More than 20 Thai senators accused of vote-buying
Article:
BANGKOK: Thailand's Election Commission accused 26 sitting senators on Monday of colluding to rig the last Senate election, an alleged vote-buying scandal that has sparked protests and could see them jailed.
The commission said it will refer the case, which allegedly involves senators allied with Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul's party, to the Supreme Court.
The 26 were among 77 people accused in the scandal, alongside 36 unsuccessful Senate candidates and 15 other political figures accused of election fraud. None was identified.
The Senate scrutinises bills passed by the lower house and appoints heads of key government bodies such as the Constitutional Court, National Anti-Corruption Commission and Election Commission.
The contested election took place in June 2024, the first such poll since a coup a decade earlier, when the senators were chosen by the military.
Rather than a direct election by Thai voters, senators were chosen by other Senate candidates to represent 20 different sectors, including justice, education, public health, industry, arts and sport.
The 200 members chosen in the three-round process included a significant number of former civil servants, military and police officers, and many who back Anutin's conservative Bhumjaithai party, according to analysts.
The commission has 60 days to file its petition to the Supreme Court, which must then decide if it wants to hear the case.
If convicted, violators face up to 10 years in prison per offence, a 200,000 baht (US$6,000) fine, or both.
The case has been rumbling on for months, amid reports that 229 people, including more than 130 senators, senior Bhumjaithai party members and other politicians, were implicated in a government investigation into election fraud.
Senior Election Commission officials did not confirm the figure at a news conference on Monday.
Hundreds of Thais marched through Bangkok on Sunday calling for the indictment of the 229 in a protest organised by accountability watchdog iLaw.
Yingcheep Atchanont, executive director of iLaw, has pledged to release troves of documents he says are from the Election Commission's investigation if the Supreme Court does not hear the case.--AFP

Title: Penang deploys vehicle with crane to remove abandoned cars
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A special vehicle is helping the Penang Island City Council (MBPP) remove abandoned vehicles that conventional tow trucks cannot handle.
MBPP mayor Datuk A. Rajendran said the "multi purpose loader with crane" was acquired in 2022 and was mainly used for abandoned where conventional tow trucks were not practical.
"The equipment is mainly used for abandoned where conventional tow trucks are not practical, such as vehicles without tyres or those positioned in a manner that prevents a tow truck from removing them," he told NST.
The equipment gained attention on social media after Kristine Teoh posted about its use, saying motorists could no longer assume that parking between two vehicles would prevent their cars from being towed.
Her post drew positive reactions, with users praising MBPP's efforts to deal with abandoned vehicles.
Rajendran said the equipment was not routinely used for ordinary illegal parking or traffic obstruction cases.
"MBPP has other enforcement vehicles specifically for conventional towing operations," he said, adding that the loader could also be used to relocate heavy municipal objects, including concrete barriers, when required.
On Aug 27, Seri Delima assemblyman Connie Tan said several abandoned vehicles had been removed over two weeks through cooperation between her office, MBPP and relevant agencies.
She said the cleanup would continue, with abandoned vehicles identified and removed location by location to return public parking spaces to the community.
Vehicle owners have been urged not to leave unwanted vehicles in public parking spaces for prolonged periods.

Title: Croatian climber who sparked 43-man Kinabalu rescue faces action
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The Croatian citizen who was rescued after falling while climbing Mount Kinabalu recently may face action after he was suspected of using an unofficial route and climbing without a permit.
Sabah Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin said Sabah Parks had lodged a police report over the incident involving Mauro Persic, 46, who is still receiving treatment.
He said the police and Sabah Parks were investigating the case to determine further action against the tourist after he recovers.
"The police and Sabah Parks are investigating the case and looking into what action should be taken. After that, perhaps once he has recovered, we will deal with it," he told a press conference on the state-level Malaysia Day Celebration here today.
Bernama reported on Sept 11 that a total of 43 search and rescue (SAR) personnel successfully brought Persic down after a five-day operation that also involved challenging terrain and rainy weather conditions.
Jafry said the climber could be fined, but this would depend on the outcome of the authorities' investigation.
He added that the incident should also serve as a lesson to the public not to use unofficial trails to climb Mount Kinabalu, as doing so could pose a safety risk.
Persic sustained injuries to his right leg and right ribs, as well as minor wounds to his hands. He received initial treatment at Timpohon Gate and being taken to Ranau Hospital for further treatment.
The rescue operation involved personnel from the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM); the Special Tactical Operation and Rescue Malaysia (STORM) and Mountain Search and Rescue (MOCSAR) team, as well as mountain guides, porters, rangers and other security agencies.– BERNAMA

Title: US blocks Iran nuclear chief from Vienna meeting
Article:
VIENNA: Iran's nuclear chief was blocked from attending an annual conference on Monday at the headquarters of the UN's nuclear agency in Vienna after US pressure, both Washington and Teheran said.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright confirmed to reporters that Washington had applied pressure to stop Mohammad Eslami from entering Austria, saying "he's a sanctioned individual and we don't want sanctioned individuals evading their sanctions."
"He asked for a waiver of the sanctions and it was denied."
Iranian state TV said Eslami and a delegation "took a regular flight to Vienna on Saturday, but were blocked on the way because of obstructions by the United States."
Behrouz Kamalvandi, a senior official from Iran's nuclear agency, accused the US of "bullying political pressure" and said the block set a precedent that would affect everybody.
The Austrian foreign ministry told AFP it had requested an exemption for Mohammad Eslami, who is covered by a UN travel ban, but that the Security Council rejected it "due to a lack of consensus."
A diplomatic source in Vienna had told AFP earlier that US pressure was behind the entry refusal.
Eslami was due to attend the annual general conference of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), the UN's nuclear watchdog, which runs until Friday.
Eslami attended last year's event and delivered a speech there on behalf of Iran, a member state of the IAEA, despite the sanctions against him already being in place.
Teheran summoned Austria's charge d'affaires in response to the decision to bar Eslami.
"The Austrian government's refusal to issue visas to the delegation of the Islamic Republic of Iran is a completely unjustified decision," foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei said at a press conference in Teheran attended by AFP.
"It is clear to us that this incident occurred under American pressure, but that does not absolve the Austrian government of responsibility."
The United States and Israel launched a war against Iran on Feb 28.
For decades, Western powers have accused the Islamic republic of seeking nuclear weapons, a claim that Teheran categorically denies.--AFP

Title: Father remanded over alleged assault of daughter at Kota Baru eatery
Article:
KOTA BARU: Police have detained a man in his 40s who allegedly kicked his daughter at an eatery in Telipot here.
Kota Baru district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Azmir Damiri said the suspect surrendered himself at the Kota Baru police station yesterday and was subsequently remanded to facilitate investigations.
"We detained the suspect yesterday after he surrendered himself. He is currently being remanded for further investigations," he said when contacted.
The case is being investigated under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001.
Police had earlier sought the man and his daughter to assist investigations after a video showing him allegedly kicking the girl went viral on social media platform Threads.
Police received a report from a member of the public about the video at about 10.24pm on Saturday.
The video, uploaded by the premises owner, showed a man allegedly acting aggressively towards a girl believed to be his daughter before kicking her.

Title: Nuenergy to invest 21MWp solar PV facilities across 49 rooftop sites
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Nuenergy Holdings Bhd will invest in developing 21 megawatt-peak (MWp) solar photovoltaic (PV) facilities across 49 rooftop sites at a government agency's premises.
Nuenergy said its wholly owned subsidiary IL Energy Sdn Bhd would undertake the investment, with the facilities forming part of the group's portfolio of owned renewable energy assets.
It said the development of the facilities across the 49 rooftop sites will be undertaken by the subsidiary of the government agency as the main engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning (EPCC) contractor.
The group said its other wholly owned unit Armani Sinar Sdn Bhd accepted a letter of award from the government agency on Sept 11, 2026, to collaborate as a strategic partner for the EPCC development of the facilities.
"As the strategic partner, Armani Sinar will provide engineering design support, establish the technical standards for the execution of the works, undertake technical reviews and carry out site verification, as well as supply the solar PV modules and solar inverters for the project," Nuenergy said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia.
The group said the project will enable the group to add the project to its portfolio of owned renewable energy assets, generating recurring energy income over the term of the offtake arrangements and broadening its earnings base beyond project-based engineering and construction income.
It said the project accepted by Armani Sinar is expected to contribute positively to the Nuenergy group's earnings and net assets per share.
The facilities are expected to be completed in the second quarter of 2027, it added.

Title: DSR Taiko, PKNP ink Mou to authenticate, certify Pahang Musang King
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: DSR Taiko Bhd plans to collaborate with the Pahang State Development Corporation (PKNP) to establish a verified origin standard and digitising export traceability for Musang King durians originating from Pahang.
The durian orchard manager said it has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with PKNP to work together on setting up special purpose vehicles (SPVs) to develop and implement an authentication, certification and verification system for the state's Musang King durians.
"The areas of collaboration under the MoU include origin authentication, labelling, traceability, certification, market development, as well as the development and promotion of 'Pahang First'," it said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia today.
DSR Taiko said the initiative would form part of the proposed Pahang Durian City (PDC), which is envisaged as a strategic research and development hub for Pahang's Musang King durian.
The detailed shareholding, governance, investment, intellectual property, commercial and operational arrangements of the SPVs would be mutually agreed upon by the parties at a later stage, the company said.
"The parties also intend to jointly engage relevant government agencies, statutory bodies, certification bodies, industry players and other stakeholders, where appropriate, in relation to the project," it said.
The MoU will remain in force for six months from the date of the MoU, unless terminated earlier in accordance with its terms, DSR Taiko said, adding that the parties may apply to extend the MoU on mutually agreed terms by giving one month's written notice before its expiry.
The company also said the MoU and its contents are not legally binding on the parties except for the confidentiality provisions, and neither party may make any claim against the other in the event of non-performance of its terms and conditions.
The MoU is not expected to have any material effect on DSR Taiko's net assets per share, gearing and earnings per share for the financial year ending Sept 30, 2026.
None of the directors, major shareholders of DSR Taiko or persons connected with them have any direct or indirect interest in the MoU, it said.

Title: Nepal mission over, Smart team members in good health
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart), which participated in the Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) mission in Nepal, arrived safely in the country at 2am today.
Smart commander Senior Fire Superintendent Abdul Manaf Che Isa said the team departed from Kathmandu at 3pm yesterday (local time) aboard a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) A400M aircraft, making a brief stopover in Kolkata, India, for refueling.
"Upon arrival at RMAF Subang Air Base, we underwent health screenings conducted by Health Ministry officials, and all 11 members involved in the mission were confirmed to be in good health," he told Bernama here today.
Earlier, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan had announced that the team was scheduled to return on Saturday or Sunday.
He stated that equipment belonging to the team, such as drones, had been handed over to rescue teams in Nepal for use in search operations for victims of flash floods and landslides in the country.
The Smart MAS01 team participating in the HADR mission arrived in the country via Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu, on Sept 5, bringing with them 12.4 tonnes of search and rescue (SAR) equipment. – BERNAMA

Title: Ringgit ends higher against most major, Asean currencies
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit appreciated against most major and Asean currencies at Monday's close, although it declined against the US dollar.
This fluctuation occurred amid rising Brent crude prices, as markets anticipated the upcoming Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) and Bank of Japan (BOJ) meetings, said an analyst.
At 6 pm, the local currency depreciated to 4.0735/0770 against the greenback from last Friday's close of 4.0685/0725.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said Brent crude oil prices are currently hovering at around US$107 per barrel, adding to inflationary pressures as markets brace for the upcoming FOMC and BOJ interest rate decisions.
"Inflationary bias would solidify the rate hike thesis this week. Following this, Asian currencies including the ringgit will remain guarded in the near term," he told Bernama.
At the close, the ringgit strengthened against the euro to 4.7008/7049 from last Friday's 4.7178/7225, appreciated against yen to 2.6355/6380 from 2.6400/6428, and inched up vis-a-vis the British pound to 5.4931/4978 from 5.4961/5015 previously.
Against its ASEAN peers, the ringgit firmed against the Singapore dollar to 3.2055/2085 from 3.2091/2125, and advanced against the Thai baht to 12.2445/2598 from 12.3072/3241.
The local note also rose against the Indonesian rupiah to 230.5/230.8 from 231.0/231.3 last week, and ticked up vis-a-vis the Philippine peso to 6.48/6.49 from 6.49/6.50 previously.

Title: Croatian climber who scaled Mount Kinabalu illegally may face fine
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 14 — The Croatian national who had to be rescued after falling while trying to ascend Mount Kinabalu on an unsanctioned route and without a permit may be slapped with a fine.
Sabah Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin said Sabah Parks had lodged a police report over the incident involving the 46-year-old Mauro Persic, who is still in recovery.
“The police and Sabah Parks are investigating the case and looking into what action should be taken. After that, perhaps once he has recovered, we will deal with it,” he told a press conference on the state-level Malaysia Day Celebration here today.
“But considering everything… maybe he will receive a fine,” he added.
Jafry said that the incident should also serve as a lesson to the public not to use unofficial trails to climb Mount Kinabalu, as doing so could pose a safety risk.
Last week, it was reported that a total of 43 search and rescue (SAR) personnel successfully brought Persic down after a five-day operation that also involved challenging terrain and rainy weather conditions.
Persic had attempted to scale the mountain from a separate, closed-off route from Mesilou, but ran into challenges, fell down and had to call authorities for help.
He had initially took part in an extreme adventure race in the Tambatuan area of Kota Belud.
During his ordeal, Persic sustained injuries to his right leg and right ribs, as well as minor wounds to his hands.
The rescue operation involved personnel from the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM); the Special Tactical Operation and Rescue Malaysia (STORM) and Mountain Search and Rescue (MOCSAR) team, as well as mountain guides, porters, rangers and other security agencies.
Persic expressed gratefulness to the team who rescued him, especially the porter who carried him down on his back, and said the adventure was “probably not” worth it but thanked the rescue team for the kindness shown to him.

Title: Sabah mulls relocation of Kota Kinabalu central market
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 14 — The Sabah government is mulling three new spots for the relocation of the Kota Kinabalu central market from the heart of the city.
Chief minister Datuk Hajiji Noor who visited and inspected two of the proposed sites – along Likas Bay and near Alamesra, said that no final decision had been made on its suitability or the location of the new market.
The third proposed site is in the area of Darau, some 20km from the city centre.
“The government has plans to relocate this central market from the middle of Kota Kinabalu, so that is why we came to see and inspect the proposed site.
“The government will consider and decide which site is suitable for us to build the new Kota Kinabalu central market,” he told reporters after visiting the site.
Hajiji said the proposed new market was envisaged as more than a conventional public market, with various activities and facilities incorporated into the development like both dry market and wet market, a cultural, local and tourism products centre, hawkers centre and fish wharf.
Hajiji visited a 40-acre piece of state land along Jalan UMS in Alamesra and the second proposed site located on a mixed-commercial land belonging to the Local Government and Housing Ministry near Kampung Likas along Tun Fuad Stephens coastal road adjacent to Anjung Selera.
Hajiji said the Kota Kinabalu City Hall (DBKK) would first prepare a working paper on the proposal before it was brought to the Cabinet for consideration and a decision, saying that the proposal was still in its early stages.
“What is important is that we ensure which site is suitable for building a fairly large and good market, not just an ordinary public market.
“The market to be built will encompass all activities near the market, as we saw at the site earlier. That is the concept,” he said.
Hajiji also said no decision had been made on what would happen to the existing central market site after the relocation.
He said any proposal for the old site would come from the city mayor.
“That proposal will come later from the city mayor on what will be done there. We don't know yet,” he said.
Hajiji also said no cost estimate was available yet, as the government was currently only assessing potential sites.
“The value has not been determined. It is only the site for now,” he said.

Title: Sabah leaders call for apology from Umno man’s remarks on Christianity
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 14 — Two Sabah leaders have called on Sepang Umno chief Datuk Noorazli Said to apologise over his controversial remarks concerning christianity and the Bible at the recent Umno general assembly.
Tenom MP Datuk Arthur Kurup said Noorazli’s remarks were “highly inappropriate” and did not reflect the maturity expected of a political leader, while Tuaran MP and Tamparuli assemblyman Datuk Wilfred Madius Tangau described the joke as “grossly inappropriate and offensive”.
Kurup, in a statement, said political differences did not give anyone the licence to make light of another person’s religion and beliefs for the sake of laughter or applause.
“Malaysia was built on the foundations of a multi-racial and multi-religious society. After more than six decades of living together as a nation, it is deeply disappointing that there are still leaders who choose to turn religion into material for political jokes.
“Politics has its limits, freedom of speech comes with responsibility, and religion is not something to be made light of,” he said.
Kurup also reminded political leaders that matters involving the 3Rs — race, religion and the royal institution — should not be touched on indiscriminately.
He said Barisan Nasional, of which Umno is a component party, was founded on principles of unity, stability and solidarity among Malaysians of different races and religions.
“We cannot speak about unity at one moment while, at another, allowing the religion of others to be turned into material for political jokes.
“We must uphold this principle consistently, not only when it benefits us,” said the BN Sabah chairman.
Tangau, meanwhile, called on Noorazli to apologise to the Catholic community over the remarks.
“Sacred Scripture, Catholic priests and religious sisters should not be sexualised or ridiculed from the stage of a major national political party,” Tangau said in a Facebook post.
He also urged Noorazli to acknowledge his “poor judgment”, withdraw the reference to Psalm 129 and offer an “unqualified public apology” to the Catholic and wider Christian community.
The controversy arose after Noorazli made a joke at the Umno general assembly on Saturday involving a priest and a nun, with its punchline attributed to Psalm 129 in the Bible.
However, the purported passage does not appear in Psalm 129.
In a Facebook post following the criticism, Noorazli said the point he was trying to convey through the joke was the importance of focus, perseverance and wisdom in achieving one's goals.
“It was never meant to insult, belittle, or demean anyone or a religion,” he said.
He said the joke was intended as an analogy and that the episode had taught him to be more cautious when using analogies in future.

Title: MACC officer denies key witness against Muhyiddin given ‘special treatment’, ‘immunity’ from own corruption case
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) did not give “special treatment” and has not struck a deal with businessman Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff in exchange for him being a key prosecution witness against former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, the High Court heard today.
MACC senior assistant commissioner Mazery Mohd Zaini, who investigated Muhyiddin’s power abuse case, confirmed this while testifying as the 29th prosecution witness in the Bersatu president’s trial here.
Under cross-examination by Muhyiddin’s lawyer Datuk Hisyam Teh Poh Teik, Mazery confirmed that Azman was a suspect in an MACC investigation in 2023 involving serious allegations of him and his associated companies KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd and Addeen Engineering Sdn Bhd soliciting and accepting bribes.
Previously, Azman, who is Bumiputera Contractors Association of Malaysia (PKBM) president, confirmed that the two companies had received RM9.35 million from several contractors.
While confirming investigations showed Azman’s companies receiving RM9.35 million from Jana Wibawa contractors, Mazery disagreed that there is a “prima facie” case that Azman had solicited and received bribes.
Mazery said he will not investigate Azman again after this, but said he did not know if the case against Azman has been closed.
Mazery disagreed that his investigation on Azman is “biased”, and also denied protecting Azman.
Hisyam: You protect Datuk Azman because he came to court to give evidence against Tan Sri.
Mazery: I disagree.
Mazery told Hisyam that he did not find it “strange” on the different outcomes for two individuals — where Azman had not been charged for receiving RM1 million from Jana Wibawa contractor Nepturis Sdn Bhd while Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad was charged for receiving RM2 million from the same company.
Mazery confirmed that Azman was not remanded during MACC investigations, but denied any special treatment was given to the businessman.
Hisyam: And I say he received special treatment from the MACC because there is a deal between MACC and Azman — testify in court, will be given immunity.
Mazery: I disagree.
Mazery later also disagreed with Hisyam’s suggestion that MACC did not take action on Azman as it needs him to come to court to be a prosecution witness against Muhyiddin.
Hisyam suggested that Azman had no choice but to cooperate with the MACC due to the businessman’s own corruption case, but Mazery disagreed.
Mazery also disagreed that MACC had used the corruption allegations against Azman as a “sword”, also disagreeing that was why Azman had agreed with everything MACC wanted him to agree in court.
Former Prime Minister, Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin is pictured at the Kuala Lumpur High Court Complex on September 2, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
This afternoon, lead prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin asked why Mazery had disagreed that the RM9.35 million were bribes to Azman.
Mazery then said that his investigations had shown a money trail where those funds were actually meant for the political party Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia.
“Because the money that entered Addeen and KCJ’s accounts are actually to be moved to party Bersatu’s account. So it is based on the trail that I made,” he said.
“Based on the money trail I carried out, the money which entered from the companies you mentioned to Addeen and KCJ were re-entered to party Bersatu’s account,” he added.
While confirming that Muhyiddin’s name did not appear in several complaints to the MACC on alleged corruption cases linked to Jana Wibawa and had only appeared in a money laundering complaint, Mazery explained that Muhyiddin was charged because of investigation findings.
“Because based on investigations that were carried out on the complaint, the investigation findings show Datuk Azman asked for donations and deposited them into party Bersatu’s account, as a ‘balasan’ (reward) for Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s helping companies to get Jana Wibawa projects. So because of that, the charges on Tan Sri were carried out,” he explained.
Earlier today, the High Court allowed Muhyiddin’s application to recall four prosecution witnesses on specific issues, saying that this was in the interest of justice.
Muhyiddin’s lawyers had this morning applied to recall those four witnesses, as the prosecution had changed its plans and decided not to call in Adam Radlan as a prosecution witness.
The four witnesses are Azman, contractors Nepturis Sdn Bhd’s Lian Tan Chuan and Mamfor Sdn Bhd’s Shahradzi Shamsuddin, and MACC assistant enforcement officer Mohd Syawaludin Said.
In this trial, Muhyiddin is facing seven charges, namely four counts of alleged power abuse to obtain RM225.3 million in bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd), and three counts of alleged money laundering involving money that Bersatu received from Bukhary Equity.
The trial before High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin is scheduled to resume tomorrow, with Mazery and the four recalled prosecution witnesses expected to take the stand.

Title: Toy-ing with the bomb squad? Suspicious object in Sri Petaling destroyed, found to contain toy blocks (VIDEO)
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — A suspicious plastic box found unattended in front of a shoplot in Bandar Baru Sri Petaling earlier today contained toy building blocks after a police bomb disposal unit was called to the scene.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Commissioner Datuk Fadil Marsus said authorities were alerted to the box at about 12.57pm after a 33-year-old woman reported the discovery.
“Initial checks found that the object had a high radiation reading, which prompted the deployment of a Bomb Disposal Unit, together with the Bukit Aman Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear and Explosive (CBRNE) Unit, to the scene for further checks and evaluation,” he said.
Representatives from the Malaysian Nuclear Agency were also present.
"The Bomb Disposal Unit then used a Recoilless Disruptor 5.0, an explosive ordnance disposal device, to destroy the suspicious object before discovering several boxes believed to contain colourful building blocks inside the plastic box," he said in a statement here.
He said further checks by the Malaysian Nuclear Agency later confirmed that there were no traces of radioactivity in the vicinity.
Fadil said the case is being investigated under Section 506 of the Penal Code for criminal intimidation.
"The public is also advised not to spread false information that could cause public unrest," he said.
Anyone with information is urged to contact the Kuala Lumpur police hotline at 03-21159999 or the Brickfields police hotline at 03-22979222 or any nearby police stations.
